newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil easier, Med cargoes add pressure.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil easier, Med cargoes add pressure.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices were easier on Tuesday as weaker barge and cargo premiums countered small gains on Benchmark gas oil futures, traders said.
They said a $10-$13 arbitrage window was drawing additional supplies from the Mediterranean and putting pressure on cargo prices in a market already suffering from thin demand.
"Some product is still finding its way east (from the Med) but 0.2 sulphur oil is becoming lengthy and finding its way up here," one trader said.
Traders said 0.2 sulphur cargo premiums slipped 50 to 75 cents a tonne to value around June IPE +50 cents cif NWE.

Low sulphur diesel cargoes fared slightly better. Quality Algerian product was asking around June IPE +$7 a tonne with some interest at around +$5.50 seen for long term restocking, while other cargoes talked June IPE +$5/+$6 a tonne cif NWE.
The key ARA barge market saw some activity at slightly weaker levels. Prompt Rotterdam liftings were reported traded at around June IPE +50 and +75 cents a tonne.
